summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and HIV presented with chills, fever, and purulent drainage from her right femoral tunneled dialysis catheter, concerning for catheter-related infection. She also reported new vaginal discharge and lower abdominal pain. Blood and catheter tip cultures confirmed MRSA infection, prompting removal of the infected catheter and placement of a new left femoral tunneled line. She completed a dose of vancomycin and was transitioned to a four-week course administered during dialysis. An echocardiogram showed no evidence of endocarditis. A venogram revealed significant IVC stenosis, which was partially treated with balloon angioplasty during replacement of the catheter. Her vaginal symptoms were evaluated and found to be non-infectious. She was restarted on midodrine for dialysis-related hypotension and counseled on adherence to her HIV and other chronic medications. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient follow-up in dermatology, primary care, and possible allergy and vascular surgery.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
Other complications due to renal dialysis device, implant, and graft
Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications
